quizzes.title: Animal Friends
quizzes.description: Fun questions about creatures big and small.

questions.q: What is the biggest animal on Earth?
questions.note: A blue whale can be longer than two school buses.

questions.q: A baby cat is called a kitten.
questions.note: Kittens open their eyes when they are about a week old.

questions.q: A caterpillar grows up to become which of these?
questions.note: Some caterpillars become moths instead of butterflies.

questions.q: Which animal is called the "King of the Jungle"?
questions.note: Lions actually live on grasslands called savannahs, not in jungles.

questions.q: What is a baby frog called?
questions.note: Tadpoles live in water and breathe through gills at first.

questions.q: How many legs does an insect have?
questions.note: Ants, bees and ladybirds all have six legs.

questions.q: Penguins can fly.
questions.note: Penguins can't fly, but they are brilliant swimmers.

questions.q: Which animal carries its baby in a pouch?
questions.note: A baby kangaroo is called a joey.

questions.q: What do giant pandas mostly eat?
questions.note: A panda can spend around half the day eating bamboo.

questions.q: What is the fastest land animal?
questions.note: A cheetah can sprint about as fast as a car on a motorway.

quizzes.title: Colours & Shapes
quizzes.description: Mix colours and count sides in this bright and simple round.

questions.q: How many sides does a triangle have?
questions.note: "Tri" means three, like in tricycle.

questions.q: What shape is round like a coin and has no corners?
questions.note: Wheels, plates and pizzas are circles too.

questions.q: What colour do you get when you mix blue and yellow?
questions.note: Red, yellow and blue are called the primary colours in painting.

questions.q: A square has four equal sides.
questions.note: A square also has four corners that are all the same.

questions.q: What colour do you get when you mix red and white?
questions.note: Adding more white makes the pink lighter.

questions.q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
questions.note: Bees build their honeycombs out of hexagons.

questions.q: A rainbow has ten colours.
questions.note: A rainbow has seven: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.

questions.q: In many countries, what shape is a stop sign?
questions.note: An octagon has eight sides, like an octopus has eight arms.

questions.q: What colour do you get when you mix red and blue?
questions.note: Also accept "violet".

questions.q: Which shape has five sides?
questions.note: A famous building in the USA called the Pentagon is shaped like one.

quizzes.title: Science Sparks
quizzes.description: Easy questions about space, nature and how things work.

questions.q: Water turns into ice at 0 degrees Celsius.
questions.note: That's the same as 32 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.q: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.note: The Sun is a star, just much closer to us than the others.

questions.q: What do plants use to make their own food?
questions.note: Plants also need water and air to make food from sunlight.

questions.q: Which planet do we live on?
questions.note: Earth is the only planet we know of that has living things.

questions.q: What do we call a scientist who studies stars and planets?
questions.note: Astronomers use telescopes to look far out into space.

questions.q: Which gas do we need to breathe in to stay alive?
questions.note: Plants give off oxygen, which is one reason they are so important.

questions.q: What pulls things down to the ground when you drop them?
questions.note: Gravity also keeps the Moon going around the Earth.

questions.q: The Moon makes its own light.
questions.note: Moonlight is really sunlight bouncing off the Moon.

questions.q: Which of your five senses do you use your nose for?
questions.note: The five senses are sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.

questions.q: Which tool helps you see tiny things up close?
questions.note: A magnifying glass is a curved lens that makes things look bigger.

quizzes.title: Once Upon a Time
quizzes.description: Famous fairy tales and much-loved cartoon characters.

questions.q: What did Cinderella leave behind at the ball?
questions.note: The prince used the slipper to find her again.

questions.q: In "Goldilocks and the Three Bears", Goldilocks eats the bears' porridge.
questions.note: She likes Baby Bear's porridge best because it's just right.

questions.q: What is the name of Mickey Mouse's girlfriend?
questions.note: Minnie first appeared alongside Mickey in 1928.

questions.q: Which fairy tale girl let down her long hair from a tall tower?
questions.note: The prince climbed up her hair to reach her.

questions.q: Who was Little Red Riding Hood going to visit?
questions.note: The big bad wolf got to Grandma's house first.

questions.q: How many dwarfs lived with Snow White?
questions.note: In the Disney film, the dwarfs include Happy, Sleepy and Grumpy.

questions.q: In "Jack and the Beanstalk", Jack swaps his cow for a bag of gold.
questions.note: Jack swaps the cow for some magic beans.

questions.q: In "The Three Little Pigs", which house could the wolf not blow down?
questions.note: The third little pig worked hardest and built the strongest house.

questions.q: What is the name of Peter Pan's fairy friend?
questions.note: Also accept "Tinkerbell".

questions.q: What kind of animal is Winnie-the-Pooh?
questions.note: His friends include Piglet, Rabbit and Eeyore the donkey.
